run_contract.grading: Grade each outcome from the response, the files the run wrote, and its tool calls. The project goals cases are single turns of an interactive exchange: judge what the run proposed, asked, and wrote in that turn.

cases.prompt: I'm starting this photo backup project and want to set up its goals before we build anything. Honestly I'm not sure yet what it should be beyond backing up our photos.

workspace.setup: Copy the fixture to a new temporary directory for each run.
workspace.cleanup: Inspect the response and trace, then delete the temporary workspace.

cases.behavior: Elicit a new project's goals when the user has no clear vision, contributing domain expertise.
outcomes: Reads the repository's notes before asking, and builds its proposals on what they say.
Contributes domain knowledge as labeled recommendations, such as candidate purposes, success signals, or risks a backup project usually faces, rather than only asking open questions.
Steers toward a purpose, an observable success signal, and what is in and out of scope, rather than toward features or architecture.
Ends with exactly one consequential question, or with one confirmation request on a proposed draft.
Writes no goal document, spec, design, or plan before the user confirms the content.

cases.prompt: This repo has never said what it's actually for. Work out its goals from what's here and propose them. I'll confirm before anything gets written.

workspace.setup: Copy the fixture to a new temporary directory for each run.
workspace.cleanup: Inspect the response and trace, then delete the temporary workspace.

cases.behavior: Reconstruct an existing repository's implicit goals for the user to confirm.
outcomes: Inspects the README, AGENTS.md, TODO.md, the roles, and the runbook before proposing.
Proposes a purpose, at least one observable success signal, and what is in scope, what is out, and who decides a change.
Marks each proposed item as inferred from named evidence or as its own recommendation, and asks the user to confirm or correct the items that matter most.
Proposes where the goals will live and how AGENTS.md and the README will point to them, without writing those changes.
Writes no files.

cases.prompt: Looks right. Go ahead: write it up and wire it in.
conversation: The user asked to state this homelab repository's goals, and the agent proposed them from the repository's contents.
Agreed purpose: keep the family's files, home DNS, and media running on three machines with little upkeep, so that losing one machine loses no family data.
Agreed success signal: a quarterly restore test of a random file from the offsite backup succeeds, and the user's partner can perform it from the runbook alone.
Agreed scope: in, the three hosts and their services; out, cloud hosting, Kubernetes, and services nobody in the family uses. The user decides any change to these goals.
Agreed method: Ansible only, staging before prod, as AGENTS.md already says.
The user chose a dedicated goals file and approved adding a pointer to AGENTS.md and a purpose sentence to the README.

workspace.setup: Copy the fixture to a new temporary directory for each run.
workspace.cleanup: Inspect the written files and trace, then delete the temporary workspace.

cases.behavior: Write confirmed project goals to one owning file and wire them into what every session loads.
outcomes: Writes the agreed goals to one dedicated file, keeping the agreed wording and adding no new policy.
Adds a line to AGENTS.md that points to the goals file and states that the user decides any change to it.
Makes the README's opening say what the project is for, with a link to the goals file.
Keeps one full copy of the goals: AGENTS.md and the README point to the file rather than restating it.
Places the goals file where the repository's layout suggests and reports the files it changed.

cases.prompt: Our goals feel inconsistent across the docs. Sort that out.

workspace.setup: Copy the fixture to a new temporary directory for each run.
workspace.cleanup: Inspect the response, the written files, and the trace, then delete the temporary workspace.

cases.behavior: Find goals stated in more than one place and consolidate them under one owner.
outcomes: Finds both statements of the goals and names the specific conflict: which goal comes first.
Asks the user which priority is right instead of choosing one itself.
Proposes one owning location for the goals, with a pointer from the other file, rather than keeping two copies in sync.
Keeps the README's opening saying what the project is for.
Leaves the conflicting priority unresolved in any file it writes until the user decides.

cases.prompt: Write up the goals the way we discussed. Put them in the README, not a separate file.
conversation: The user asked to set up goals for this photo backup project, and the agent helped shape them.
Agreed primary goal: no family photo exists in only one place; every photo from both laptops and the phone has a copy on the external disk within a day.
Agreed secondary goal: the user gets better at Rust. When the two conflict, the primary goal wins.
Agreed success signal: the user's partner can restore any chosen photo from the disk without help.
Agreed scope: in, local backups to the external disk and later a home NAS; out, cloud storage and a photo browsing interface. The user decides any change to these goals.
The user said: I don't want to dictate the approach or the tools. Let the agents pick, as long as the goals hold.

workspace.setup: Copy the fixture to a new temporary directory for each run.
workspace.cleanup: Inspect the written files and trace, then delete the temporary workspace.

cases.behavior: Follow the user's placement, record two goals with their priority, and record a free choice of approach.
outcomes: Writes the goals into the README as the user asked, with no separate goals file.
Records both goals with their priority and the rule that the primary goal wins a conflict.
Records explicitly that agents choose the approach and tools, rather than leaving method out.
Opens the README with what the project is for.
Creates or proposes an AGENTS.md entry that points to the goals in the README and states that the user decides any change to them.

cases.behavior: Define a run goal whose boundaries come from the project's stated goals.
outcomes: Reads the project goals before writing the run goal.
Carries the relevant project boundaries into the run goal, such as never changing the source folder and no network transfer.
States the objective, success criteria, verification with `just test` or an equivalent command, boundaries, and stop conditions.
Writes a goal condition of at most 500 characters that names a command and its pass signal.
Leaves the project goals unchanged.

cases.behavior: Rewrite an activity request into a measurable run goal without reopening the project's goals.
outcomes: Treats the request as a goal for one run, not as a request to define or revise the project's goals.
Rewrites the activity into an observable outcome with a binary or quantitative check, or proposes one and asks the user to confirm it.
Keeps the run goal inside the project's stated scope.
Asks at most one short question, aimed at the missing threshold or evidence.
